title: Master Hanshan’s Buddha-Recitation and Rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss
author: Zhanran
excerpt: 6. Vigorously advocating: all Dharma-gates should return to the Pure Land

inline.s: Because Master Hanshan’s physical body rests alongside that of the Sixth Chan Patriarch at Caoxi, it has always been thought that Master Hanshan was merely a patriarch of the Chan school and not a patriarch of the Pure Land school. (Master Yongming and Master Chewu were both Chan patriarchs and were also honored as Pure Land patriarchs.)
In fact, Master Hanshan was reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss through Buddha-recitation,
and he vigorously advocated that all Dharma-gates should return to the Pure Land
. In both the actual practice of Buddha-recitation and the propagation of the Pure Land, he attained the most outstanding accomplishments, and he is listed in the Records of Pure Land Sages,
so he certainly should be regarded as a Pure Land patriarch
The evidence is set forth below:

Master Hanshan’s mother reverently worshiped the great being Avalokiteshvara all her life. One night she dreamed that Avalokiteshvara entered her home carrying a boy; the mother joyfully took the boy in her arms, and from then on she was pregnant. At midnight on the twelfth day of the tenth month of the twenty-fifth year of the Jiajing reign of Emperor Shizong of the Ming dynasty (
), a baby wrapped in a white double-layered placenta was born. When the placenta was peeled away and the baby washed, an extraordinary fragrance filled the entire room.

When the Master was nine, he was studying at a monastery and heard a monk there say that reciting the Avalokiteshvara Sūtra (the Universal Gate Chapter of the Lotus Sūtra on Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva) could rescue one from all the sufferings and calamities of the world. He was overjoyed, asked the monk for a copy, and read it with single-hearted devotion until he could recite it from memory. His mother often burned incense and bowed before Avalokiteshvara, and whenever he was at home he would join her in worship. One day he said to his mother, “Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva has a sūtra in one fascicle.” His mother had never heard of it, and he at once recited the whole of it for her. Delighted, she said: “Where did you get this? Your reciting voice is just like an old monk’s in the temple!”

blocks.text: 2. Reciting the Buddha, Seeing the Buddha

inline.s: When the Master was twelve, he heard a monk say: “Abbot Xilin of Bao’en Temple in Jinling practiced all his life and was a renowned great worthy.” He resolved to follow Monk Xilin to study the Buddha Dharma. At his firm insistence, his parents sent him to Bao’en Temple. When he arrived, many people, on seeing him, marveled and felt he was sure to achieve great things in the future. Monk Xilin received him in the abbot’s quarters and said with great delight: “This child has an extraordinary character; it would be a great pity for him to become merely an ordinary monk!”

Monk Xilin at once chose the most learned among his disciple-grandsons to teach him specially. He first studied the Lotus Sūtra and, after only three months, could recite it fluently. Studying earnestly for two years, he could recite from memory all the commonly circulated sūtras and treatises. Seeing his rapid progress, Monk Xilin said happily: “This child can be taught; we must not waste his time.” So he engaged a teacher well-versed in the Four Books and Five Classics to instruct him. The teacher had him first study the Four Books and Five Classics, and later the doctrines of the hundred schools, the historical classics such as the Zuo Commentary and the Records of the Grand Historian, and classical prose, poetry, songs, and rhapsodies.
The Master,
in his nineteenth year,
respectfully asked Monk Xilin to tonsure him, and formally left home.
From then on he

devoted himself single-mindedly to reciting the name of Amitabha Buddha as his practice. After reciting ceaselessly day and night for several days, he suddenly dreamed one night that Amitabha Buddha appeared in the sky, just at the place where the sun sets. The Buddha he saw in the dream was clearly visible in all his solemn marks and his halo of light
The Master reverently prostrated, touching his head to the Buddha’s feet, his heart gazing upon the Buddha with unceasing fondness
He further prayed to see Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva and Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva, and the two Bodhisattvas at once revealed their upper bodies. After this dream, the
Western
Three Sages frequently appeared shining before his eyes, and his body and mind were steeped in the joy of the Dharma.

In Master Hanshan’s twentieth

year, Master Yungu held a grand Chan retreat at Tianjie Temple, gathering fifty-three of the nation’s most renowned and virtuous monks. Master Yungu had always thought highly of Master Hanshan, and this time he strongly encouraged him to attend.
When the Master began to apply himself in the meditation hall,
because he did not know how to investigate,
he felt very distressed.
So he

respectfully came before Master Yungu, offered incense, and bowed, requesting instruction. Master Yungu taught him the gong’an of examining the true reality of Buddha-recitation (investigative Buddha-recitation) — that is, taking the single recitation “Amitabha Buddha” as a huatou, to investigate who it is that recites the Buddha. Hearing Master Yungu’s instruction, he investigated with single-minded devotion, his thought never wavering. Throughout those three months, it was as if he were in a dream: he was utterly unaware of the fellow practitioners around him, and knew nothing of the affairs of daily life

The eighth Pure Land patriarch, Master Lianchi, also attained accomplishment through the devoted practice of investigative Buddha-recitation.
The Stele Inscription of Master Lianchi says:
“At first, the Master set out on foot to visit teachers,
gaining power from investigative Buddha-recitation
, and thereupon opened the single gate of the Pure Land, embracing the three grades of capacity, and advocated it with the utmost vigor.”
(Translation: At first, Master Lianchi traveled on foot to pay respects to good spiritual teachers in every direction,
gaining power from investigative Buddha-recitation
, and at this point opened the single gate of the Pure Land to embrace the superior, middling, and inferior capacities, and advocated it with the utmost vigor.) It also says:
(Master Lianchi)
At the time of his death, half a month in advance, entered the city to take leave of his disciples and old acquaintances.”
This shows that Master Lianchi knew the time of his death at least half a month in advance.
When Master Hanshan was thirty, he attained the Way at Mount Wutai. In the Author’s Preface and Chronological Biography, the Master wrote:
One day, after the morning gruel, while walking in meditation, I suddenly stood still
(suddenly entered samādhi while standing)

, and saw neither body nor mind, only one great treasury of brilliant light, perfect, clear, and still, like a great round mirror in which the mountains, rivers, and great earth were reflected. When I awoke
(came out of samādhi)
, all was luminous
(all was one expanse of light)

, and searching for body and mind, I found them utterly unobtainable. Then I uttered this verse: ‘In a flash the wild mind ceased to race; within and without, the faculties and objects all grew clear. Turning over, I broke through the empty space — the myriad forms in profusion arise and vanish here.’ From then on, within and without all was clear and still; sounds, forms, and appearances no longer posed any obstruction, and all my former doubts were at once dispelled. Looking at the cooking pot, I saw that dust had already gathered on it; living alone with no companion, I had no one to ask, and so did not know how long it had been
(returning indoors, I saw the rice pot already covered with dust; living alone with no companion and no one to ask, I did not know how many days had passed)

blocks.text: 5. The Buddha-Recitation Samādhi Reaches Its Sublime Stage

inline.s: According to the
Dream Journey Collection
Author’s Preface and Chronological Biography:
at the age of thirty-three, Master Hanshan pricked his tongue and, mixing the blood with gold paste, wrote out the Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
Regardless of the size of each stroke, with every stroke he wrote, he recited the Buddha once in his heart

. Monks and laypeople touring the mountain who came to Miaode Hermitage at Mount Wutai all insisted on seeing the Master and asking him to expound the Dharma. Although the Master’s hand never stopped writing, he still did not fail to respond and converse with them. To everyone who came seeking instruction, he would speak a few words. To eminent friends and old acquaintances, he would respectfully invite them to sit on the meditation platform and converse with them about the Dharma, while at the same time continuing to write the sūtra without hindrance. Every day the Master wrote in this way, and although people came and went, no sign of disturbance could be detected in his mind. When the venerable literary elders of the neighborhood heard of this, they were astonished and could hardly believe it. One day the elders, leading many disciples, came to the Master’s quiet room, wanting to verify what was really going on. They deliberately tried all sorts of ways to distract him. When the Master had finished a passage, they compared it with the original text, and indeed there was not the slightest error; only then were they convinced that the Master’s attainment was extraordinary. Still greatly puzzled, they went to ask Master Miaofeng: “How can Master Hanshan use his mind on many things at once?” Master Miaofeng replied:
My elder Dharma-brother has fully matured in the Buddha-recitation samādhi!
Original text
In the sixth year
(the sixth year of the Wanli reign)
, the wuyin year,
I was thirty-three. With single purpose
(single-mindedness)
I wrote out the sūtra.
Regardless of the size of each stroke, with every stroke I recited the Buddha once

. When monks and laypeople touring the mountain came, I always had the attendant announce them. Though my hand never ceased writing, I still did not fail to respond. To everyone who came to inquire after me, I would speak a few words. To eminent friends and old acquaintances, I would invite them to sit on the meditation platform, conversing without neglect while not hindering my writing. Writing against the model, I made no mistake. Each day was as usual, without the slightest sign of movement or stillness. The neighboring venerable elders privately found this extraordinary, and leading a number of people came to test me, deliberately creating disturbance. When I finished writing, they read it and were truly convinced. They then asked Master Miao: “How can Master Yin be like this?” Master Miao said:
my friend has entered this samādhi
(the Buddha-recitation samādhi)
to full maturity
See
Dream Journey Collection
· Author’s Preface and Chronological Biography
Master Hanshan’s Dream Journey Collection
Letter to Chan Master Xingchu Yuan on Writing Out the Sūtra says:
The old man
(Master Hanshan’s self-reference)
formerly lived at Mount Wutai, and once pricked blood and mixed it with gold paste to write out the great Avataṃsaka Sūtra. In the midst of the writing,
regardless of the size, length, or shape of each stroke, with every stroke I recited the Buddha once

. Stroke after stroke, the light of the mind streamed forth; thought after thought, without interruption or forgetfulness, without error or omission. After a long time, whether writing or not writing, even in dreams, it all became one continuous whole. Thus amid all circumstances, however agitated, noisy, and disturbing, my mind remained clear and still,
attaining the liberation-gate of being free and unobstructed in all circumstances
, so that all I saw and heard was nothing other than the true sūtra appearing before me.”

blocks.text: 6. Vigorously Advocating: All Dharma-Gates Should Return to the Pure Land

inline.s: In the Ming dynasty in which Master Hanshan lived, the Chan school, as ever, was the mainstream of Buddhism. Under such circumstances, Master Hanshan not only recited the Buddha and sought rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss himself, but, with great foresight, vigorously advocated that all Dharma-gates should return to the Pure Land. In the Dream Journey Collection
Preface to Returning to the Pure Land, the Master taught:
The single gate of the Pure Land
embraces all three grades of capacity, admitting the sudden and the gradual alike, excluding no capacity whatsoever; it is what is called leaping horizontally beyond the three realms,
and is the most supreme Dharma-gate
. Among the patriarchs of old and those who realized the mind,
there was not one who did not take this as their final refuge
, such as Nāgārjuna
(Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna)
and Aśvaghoṣa
(Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa)
, who praised and extolled it with the utmost vigor.”
He also said:
Among those of the highest capacity in the Chan school, there is none who does not return to the Pure Land.
In the Dream Journey Collection
On the Practice of the Pure Land Dharma-Gate, Master Hanshan taught:
“The Buddha taught that for the practice of escaping birth and death there are many skillful gates,
but only reciting the Buddha and seeking rebirth in the Pure Land
is the most direct and essential
The Commentary on Master Hanshan’s Chronological Biography records:
“Patriarch Hanshan once instructed Zheng
(Fuzheng)

: In reciting the Buddha, if one is unwilling to apply a wholehearted resolve but merely recites amid floating thoughts, then in reality the latent habits flowing in the store consciousness are not seen at all, and so one never sees a single thought of the recitation settle down.
If Buddha-recitation gains power, it surpasses even investigating ‘the cypress tree’ or ‘the dried shit-stick.’

blocks.text: 7. In His Later Years, Single-Minded Pure Land Practice

inline.s: In his later years
(the Master was then seventy-four)
Master Hanshan wrote in a letter:
Now, in seclusion
(in closed-door retreat)
, all Chan ways and Buddha Dharma I have put on a high shelf, simply keeping to plainness
(single-mindedly reciting the Buddha; “keeping to plainness” here means no longer investigating Chan or studying the teachings)
I specially emulate Duke Yuan
(Master Huiyuan)
in his six periods
(twelve hours)
lotus water-clock
(the “lotus clock” is the lotus water-clock; it was made by Huiyao, a disciple of Huiyuan, the first Pure Land patriarch, who used a lotus as a clepsydra to measure time at the Lushan practice site)
, using incense in place of flowers
(I use burning incense in place of the lotus water-clock to measure time, reciting the Buddha twelve hours each day)
. For several months now,
body and mind have of themselves arrived at the Land of Bliss
(Dream Journey Collection
· Reply to Grand Historian Qian Shouzhi)
The Master’s Chronological Biography records:
(the Wanli reign)
In the forty-seventh year, the jiwei year, I was seventy-four. ...... On the full moon of the eighth month
(the fifteenth day of the eighth month)
, I closed my door and retired from affairs, emulating Duke Yuan, marking the six periods with burning incense in place of the water-clock,
devoting myself single-mindedly to the Pure Land practice

blocks.text: 8. At Death, Reciting the Buddha and Being Reborn

inline.s: Master Hanshan passed away on the thirteenth day of the tenth month of the third year of the Tianqi reign (
), at the age of seventy-eight. According to the Commentary on Master Hanshan’s Chronological Biography:
On the twelfth day of the tenth month,
which was Master Hanshan’s
birthday,
monastic and lay
disciples gathered in great numbers to
celebrate his birthday
. Prefect Zhang Sanxing of Shaoyang entered the mountain to present a purple silk Chan robe, to
offer the Master his birthday congratulations
and the two of them
sat
and
conversed
the whole day
. The next
morning (the thirteenth day of the tenth month), Master Hanshan
put
on
the Chan robe that Sir Zhang had given, and bade
him
farewell.
At noon,
Sir Zhang departed,
and Master Hanshan
at once called an attendant to bring pure water to rinse his mouth,
saying
: “Today I cut off the entangling vines.”
Then he
called for hot water, bathed, and changed his robes
. After that, he bade
the assembly gather around and recite the Buddha. The Master
admonished them
Do not
be alarmed; you must follow
the Buddha’s regulations, and do not wear mourning hemp.
Do not
weep,
but
recite the Buddha single-mindedly.” At the hour of shen (three o’clock in the afternoon),
Master Hanshan
passed away sitting upright.
That
night, a ray of light illumined the sky and flocks of birds cried mournfully;
monastics and laity
wailed in grief, their voices shaking the mountain valleys.
Master Hanshan
passed away;
thereafter
he remained seated upright for three days, his face fair, his lips ruddy, and his hands and feet
soft and supple,
as though in meditative absorption.
After Master Hanshan

passed away, his disciples escorted his physical body to Lushan. Because Lushan’s climate is damp and gloomy, the attendant Fushan built a stupa courtyard and enshrined the Master’s bodily reliquary on the stupa.

Eleven years later, fierce tigers caused trouble on Lushan, and Fayun Temple at Wuru Peak was in danger. Fearing the stupa site was unsafe, Fushan respectfully brought out the Master’s bodily reliquary and saw that half of the reliquary’s protective covering had been gnawed by insects and ants. Not daring to bury it, he sealed it back in the stupa as before.

Another nine years passed, and the Lingnan disciples Chen Zongbo, Liu Qixiang, and others, entrusted by the Buddhist community of Caoxi, went to Lushan to escort the Master back to Caoxi. When the Master’s physical body was being carried to Meiling, they happened to meet Song Zhaoming, the newly appointed Guangdong commander-in-chief
(a title for the regional military commander)
, who ordered his soldiers to carry the reliquary by cart and personally escorted it to Caoxi.

Only a few months after taking office, Song Zhaoming came again to Caoxi. By then the disciples guarding the reliquary, Guangcheng and Cili, seeing that the reliquary chamber had a crack, secretly chiseled a small hole in the crack and peered inside. They saw the Master’s body seated upright as in life and wished to open the reliquary chamber, but their hearts wavered with hesitation. When Song Zhaoming learned of it, he drew his saber and split open the crack. He saw the Master seated in full-lotus posture, as majestic as in life, his fingernails and hair still growing, his skin still ruddy, his robes and shoes as fresh as new. Just then a gust of wind arose, and the robes suddenly scattered like clouds breaking and stars dispersing, drifting and dancing on the wind; the local people gathered up the fragments and took them as auspicious tokens.
At that very moment a monk suddenly appeared, asking to use the Indian
(ancient Indian)

method to protect the Master’s body. With the assembly’s consent, he smeared the Master’s body with powdered Hainan sandalwood, like lacquer. Having finished applying it, the monk departed on his own.

During the Master’s lifetime, a devout young woman of Caoxi had vowed to embroider a thousand-Buddha robe to offer to the Master. Fearing her breath might be impure, she wrapped her mouth in yellow silk while embroidering. When the robe was completed, however, the Master had already been placed in his reliquary, so the robe was stored in a chest at Baolin. Now the robe was brought out again and draped over the Master’s body; although twenty years had passed, it shone brilliantly, as if newly made. The disciples enshrined the Master’s body for veneration in the old stupa courtyard, naming it Hanshan Temple, about half a li from Nanhua Temple, where the Sixth Patriarch’s body resides.
(For the above events, see
Commentary on Master Hanshan’s Chronological Biography

blocks.text: 10. Returning by the Power of Past Vows

inline.s: Master Xingce (1628–1682, the tenth Pure Land patriarch), a native of Yixing in Jiangsu, bore the lay surname Jiang and the courtesy name Jieliu. His father, Jiang Quanchang, was versed in both Confucianism and Buddhism and was a close and trusted friend of Master Hanshan. Five years after Master Hanshan passed away, Jiang Quanchang dreamed that Master Hanshan, leaning on his ringed staff, walked into the inner chamber, and then Xingce was born; hence he was given the name Menghan (Dreaming of Hanshan). As he grew up, his parents died one after another, and he gave rise to the resolve to leave the world. At the age of twenty-three
, at Li’an Temple in Wulin
(west of Hangzhou, Zhejiang)
he left home under Venerable Wen of Ruo’an. He practiced the “never-lying-down” discipline
(not sleeping at night, sitting in full-lotus posture, either reciting the Buddha or investigating Chan, cross-legged all day, without distinction of day or night)
for a full five years, and thereby suddenly and thoroughly realized the fundamental source of all dharmas.
After Venerable Wen passed away, Xingce
the Master

at Bao’en Temple met his fellow practitioner, Dharma Master Ying of Xi’an, who urged him to practice the Pure Land karma. Later he met Dharma Master Qiaoshi of Qiantang, who guided him to read the teachings of the Tiantai school. He then entered a quiet room together with Qiaoshi to practice the Lotus Samādhi
The wisdom of past lives was thereby suddenly opened, and he thoroughly realized the essence of the Tiantai teachings.
In the second year of Kangxi (1663), he built a thatched hut
on

a small plot of land in the Xixi River at Mount Fahua in Hangzhou, devoting himself solely to the Pure Land Dharma-gate, and therefore named the place where he lived “Fu-lian Hermitage” (Lotus-Calyx Hermitage)
(fu fū, meaning flower calyx)
. In the ninth year of Kangxi (1670), he took up residence at Puren Cloister on Mount Yu and advocated the founding of a Pure Land lotus society, and followers gathered like clouds from
all directions
Xingce
the Master

resided at Puren Cloister for thirteen years, until he was reborn in the Pure Land on the ninth day of the seventh month of the twenty-first year of Kangxi (1682), at the age of fifty-five. At that time there was a man named Sun Han who fell ill and died
After a day and a night he revived, saying: “I was seized by the ghost officers of the underworld and bound within the hall of King Yama
In the darkness, I suddenly saw a brilliant light illuminating the heavens, with fragrant flowers filling the empty sky
King Yama prostrated himself on the ground to welcome ‘the Master Who Returns to the West’
. I
asked who the Master was, and King Yama replied
Master Xingce!
’ I
was released and sent back because of

the light shining from Master Xingce.” On the same day, a son of the Wu family also died of illness and, reviving after a night, related what he had seen, exactly the same as Sun Han’s account. (See the Records of Pure Land Sages)
Master Yinguang praised him, saying:
“Hanshan’s past vows were not yet repaid, so he appeared again as Jieliu
(Master Xingce)
(Collected Writings of Master Yinguang · The Tenth Pure Land Patriarch of the Qing, Master Xingce of Puren Temple on Mount Yu)
